Brightwell Hospitality Lobby Refresh
Project brief, version 3
Goals

Refresh the arrival experience in three Brightwell hotel lobbies so they read as one brand while keeping a local character at each property. Guests should find the reception desk within ten seconds of entering.
Properties
Brightwell River North, 412 N Clark St (148 rooms)
Brightwell Midway, 5600 S Cicero Ave (96 rooms)
Brightwell Lakefront, 1200 S Lake Shore Dr (210 rooms, reopening in November)
Audience
Business travelers on weekdays, families and event guests on weekends. Lakefront also hosts conference groups of up to 300 people.
Budget
Design fees and furniture, fixtures and equipment for all three lobbies are budgeted at $1,260,000 to $1,450,000, excluding construction.
Order of work
River North: design development in July, install in October
Midway: design development in August, install in December
Lakefront: design development in September, install in January
Milestones
July 28: concept presentation to Alicia Brandt and the Brightwell leadership team
August 21: design development sign-off for River North
September 30: material selections locked for all three properties
October 19 to 30: River North install
Constraints
Lobbies stay open to guests throughout the work. Loud work is limited to 9:00 to 4:00, and each install phase keeps a clear path from the entrance to the elevators.

Harbor Street Cafe Menu Redesign
Brief for the menu and table cards
Background
Harbor Street Cafe, 2217 W Chicago Ave, is a 40-seat neighborhood cafe owned by Omar Haddad. The current menu is a laminated sheet that has not changed since 2021.
Deliverables
Folded menu, 11 x 17 in, printed on uncoated 100 lb cover stock
Table cards for daily specials, 4 x 6 in, 50 copies
Chalkboard lettering guide for the counter
Direction
Warm, hand-drawn and a little irreverent. Keep the coffee cup illustration on the front cover, redrawn so it prints cleanly at small sizes.
Schedule
Round 1 concepts: April 10
Round 2 revisions: May 1
Final files to Pressworks Chicago: June 5
Menu copy and prices come from Omar. Copy is not final until he signs off in writing.

Omar wants a printed proof before approving the run of 500 menus.

Case Study: Brightwell Hospitality

Brightwell Hospitality operates three hotels across Chicago, each with a lobby renovated at a different time by a different designer. Guests told Brightwell the properties felt like three unrelated brands. In 2026 Brightwell asked Lakeshore Design to bring the lobbies together without erasing what made each property feel local. We started with the arrival sequence, timing how long guests took to find the reception desk. The result is a shared system of materials, lighting and signage, adapted to each building.
The challenge
All three lobbies had to stay open during the work, and the Lakefront property was reopening on a fixed date.
Our approach
A kit of parts: one reception desk design in three sizes, a common palette of oak, terrazzo and brass, and local art commissioned for each lobby.
Results
Time to find reception fell from 24 seconds to 9 at River North in the first month after install.
Render images are pending client approval and are not included in this draft.
Case Study: Harbor Street Cafe
Harbor Street Cafe had a menu that customers loved to talk about and hated to read.
The brief
A new folded menu, table cards and a chalkboard system the staff could update without us.
What we made
A hand-drawn identity built around the cafe's coffee cup, a menu grid that fits 40 items without crowding, and a lettering guide for the counter chalkboard.
Outcome
Omar reports that breakfast orders include a drink 20 percent more often since the redesign.
